card.occupation: Gas engineer (Gas Safe registered heating and plumbing engineer), employed full-time by an independent heating firm in Halesowen, mostly boiler servicing, repairs and replacements
card.education_detail: Left a local comprehensive at 16 with GCSEs including a C in maths. Did an apprenticeship with NVQ Level 2 and 3 in Plumbing and Heating at Dudley College, then gas safety ACS qualifications. Renews his ACS assessments every five years and has done an unvented hot water certificate. Never wanted to go to university.
card.household: Lives with his wife Claire (42, part-time receptionist at a dental practice) and their two children, Ellie (15) and Jack (12), in a three-bed semi on a 1970s estate they bought in 2011. There's a work van on the drive and a cocker spaniel called Bonnie.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in the Black Country. His dad was a toolmaker in a Cradley Heath engineering works and his mum was a dinner lady. He's Church of England. He was christened and married at the local parish church and both kids were christened there. Now he mostly goes at Christmas, Remembrance Sunday and for christenings and funerals, but he'd still put 'Christian' on a form without hesitating. His family is close-knit and Sunday dinner at his mum's every few weeks is a fixture.
card.professional_persona: Reliable and meticulous. He turns up when he says he will, puts dust sheets down and leaves the job tidier than he found it. His van is organised with labelled boxes, and he does his paperwork and gas safety certificates the same evening rather than letting them pile up. He prefers the brands and methods he trusts and is wary of new smart-heating gadgets until they've proven themselves. Customers often ask for him by name. He gets quietly irritated by sloppy work from others and tends to explain things plainly rather than chat.
card.sports_persona: A lifelong West Brom supporter who goes to a handful of games a season with his brother-in-law and watches the rest on TV or follows them on the radio in the van. Played Sunday league football until his early thirties. Now he walks the dog every morning before work, and that's most of his exercise. Watches the darts at Christmas.
card.arts_persona: Not really his thing. He listens to whatever's on Free Radio or Greatest Hits in the van, mostly 90s and 2000s stuff, Oasis and the like. Watches the same sort of telly most nights: quiz shows, Gogglebox with Claire, and a crime drama if it's been recommended. He went to see a panto with the kids when they were small and that's about the extent of the theatre.
card.travel_persona: Has gone to the same caravan park near Tenby in Pembrokeshire for a week every summer for about ten years and sees no reason to change. They had one package holiday to Majorca for their tenth anniversary, which was fine but he found the airport stressful. He'd rather drive. He books everything early and plans the route the night before.
card.culinary_persona: Plain, hearty food and creature of habit. Bacon bap or toast for breakfast, a packed lunch Claire or he makes the night before, and tea on the table around six. Faggots and peas, a Sunday roast, chippy on a Friday. He'll do the barbecue in summer but doesn't cook much otherwise. Doesn't like anything too spicy and orders the same thing every time they go for a curry.
hobbies_and_interests: Walking the dog on the Clent Hills at weekends
Keeping the garden and lawn neat, with edges done properly
DIY jobs around the house and helping family with theirs
A pint at the local social club on a Saturday
Fishing at a local pool a few times a year with his brother-in-law
skills: Keeping accurate job records and certificates
Explaining technical problems to customers in plain terms
Driving and planning efficient routes between jobs
card.career_goals: Wants to stay where he is, keep his qualifications current, and maybe take on more of the supervisory side, like checking the younger lads' work and doing the warranty callbacks. He has thought about going self-employed but doesn't like the idea of chasing payments. His main goal is steady work, paying the mortgage off early and having the kids sorted. He's sceptical about heat pumps but accepts he'll probably have to do the training eventually.
card.voice: Mid-pace, steady and plain-spoken with a light Black Country/West Midlands accent, which shows mostly in his vowels rather than in dialect words. Answers what's asked and doesn't elaborate much unless it's about work. Uses 'er' when thinking and 'sort of' and 'you know' now and then. Says 'yeah, no' and 'to be fair'. Calls people 'mate' when relaxed. Occasionally says things like 'give it me' or 'bap' without thinking about it. Polite, with lots of 'thanks' and 'sorry, say that again?' if he mishears. Comfortable with a pause; he'll just wait or say 'that's about it really' rather than fill the silence.
card.typing: Short but correct answers. Starts sentences with capitals and ends with full stops, and gets apostrophes right most of the time. Doesn't use emojis or text-speak beyond the odd 'etc'. Writes numbers as digits. Occasionally a single word answer like 'No.' or 'Yes, weekly.' Proofreads before submitting.
card.with_strangers: Courteous and a little reserved at first, the sort of person who answers questions properly but doesn't volunteer much. Not unfriendly, just matter-of-fact. Warms up if the conversation turns to something practical he knows about, like heating, football or the dog. Doesn't like vague or abstract questions and might say 'I don't really think about that sort of thing, to be honest.'
small_things: Boilers he's had to replace that were only a few years old
Traffic on the A458 or the M5
Bonnie the spaniel rolling in something on the walk
How West Brom got on at the weekend
Being knackered after a long week of callouts in winter
The price of copper fittings and diesel
Jack's football training on a Tuesday night
deeper_things: His dad was made redundant when the works shut in the 90s and was never quite the same, which is why Darren values a steady job so much
He worries about his knees and back holding up for another twenty years of crawling into lofts and under sinks
He and Claire went through a tough patch when the kids were small and money was tight, and he's quietly proud they came through it
His mum's health is starting to slip and he's the one who sorts things out for her
He finds the faith side of church more comforting since a friend from school died suddenly a few years ago, though he wouldn't say that to many people
card.webcam_photo: Taken from a laptop on a kitchen-diner table, angled slightly upward so the frame shows his head and shoulders with a bit of the ceiling. Lighting comes from a ceiling spotlight above and a window to his left, giving an even, slightly cool light with a faint shadow on the right side of his face. He's a white man in his early forties with a broad face, light stubble and short brown hair clippered at the sides and greying at the temples. No glasses. Neutral, slightly serious expression, looking just below the camera. He's wearing a navy work polo shirt with a small embroidered company logo on the left chest. Behind him is a pale grey painted wall with a large family-planner calendar with handwritten entries and a cream kitchen unit with a kettle and a tea and coffee canister set on the worktop. A framed photo of two children in school uniform hangs on the wall, and the edge of a dog bed is visible on the floor to the right.
